slides.title: Section 1 Reflections
slides.after: 1.3 · SiP: From Intent to Future Reality
slides.notes:
§SECTION 1 REFLECTIONS

§HOW TO USE THIS SLIDE:

§1. Show the slide and read the two prompts aloud.
1.1 Reflection — Strategy Architecture: "Which part of your organisation's strategy architecture is least well defined today? What is the consequence?"
1.2 Reflection — Strategy Intent: "From your assigned executive leader perspective: which dimension (WHAT, WHY, HOW, WHEN) is least clearly defined in your organisation's current strategy? What would clarifying it change?"

§2. Say what the reflections are for.
Point learners to the portal section that they will be required to complete with as much depth as possible. The reflections build the learning portfolio they receive at the end of the programme.
Say: "You write these reflections on the portal after the teaching, with as much depth as you can."

§3. Set the standard for 1.1.
Say: "Name one concept from the nine, give evidence from your own organisation, and name one consequence you have seen: what the gap costs, slows down or leaves undecided."
Deepen, say: "Strategy begins with an accurate understanding of present reality. Leaders who avoid difficult information protect their comfort at the expense of the institution. Name the true condition without minimising it."
(Insight: An honest baseline. Source: Journal, 4 August 2026 — Professional Insights: Strategy)

§4. Set the standard for 1.2.
Say: "Answer from your assigned executive leader perspective. Name one dimension, and say what clarifying it would change."
Tell participants: they can start from the dimension they named in the show of hands.

§5. Take one or two first thoughts aloud.
This lets participants hear the depth you are asking for.

§6. Bridge to Section 2.
Say: "We now have the three building blocks: the architecture, the intent and the picture of success. Section 2 asks why the Strategy Intent and SiP matter once they are defined."

§ON THE PORTAL, AFTER THE TEACHING:
Participants write the two reflections in Section 1 of the participant file: 1.1 Reflection — Strategy Architecture and 1.2 Reflection — Strategy Intent.

slides.title: Section 2 Reflections
slides.notes:
§SECTION 2 REFLECTIONS

§HOW TO USE THIS SLIDE:

§1. Show the slide and read the prompt aloud.
2.1 Reflection — Three Functions: "Which of the three functions is weakest in your organisation today? What happens as a result?"

§2. Say what the reflection is for.
Point learners to the portal section that they will be required to complete with as much depth as possible. The reflections build the learning portfolio they receive at the end of the programme.
Say: "You write this reflection on the portal after the teaching, with as much depth as you can."

§3. Set the standard.
Say: "Name one function only: Strategic Alignment, Decision Filter or Execution Coherence. Describe a real situation in which the weakness showed: a decision, a meeting, a hand-off between functions. Then give the result for the organisation."

§4. Read the room.
Take a show of hands for each function and say what the pattern in the room is.

§5. Bridge to Section 3.
Say: "We know what the Strategy Intent and SiP are for. Section 3 looks closely at the SiP itself: what success looks like inside each domain, and what happens when one domain dominates the picture."

§ON THE PORTAL, AFTER THE TEACHING:
Participants write the reflection in Section 2 of the participant file: 2.1 Reflection — Three Functions.

slides.title: Section 3 Reflections
slides.notes:
§SECTION 3 REFLECTIONS

§HOW TO USE THIS SLIDE:

§1. Show the slide and read the prompt aloud.
3.1 Reflection — SiP Indicators: "From your assigned executive leader role: which SiP domain shows the most significant gaps in your organisation right now? What is the primary cause?"

§2. Say what the reflection is for.
Point learners to the portal section that they will be required to complete with as much depth as possible. The reflections build the learning portfolio they receive at the end of the programme.
Say: "You write this reflection on the portal after the teaching, from your assigned executive leader role, with as much depth as you can."

§3. Set the standard.
Say: "Name one SiP domain. Point to the indicators that show the gap: which Signal of Absence did you recognise? Then give one primary cause."
Listen for: a condition given as a cause, such as "we are under-resourced". Ask: "Which decision, structure or habit produces the gap?"

§4. Say why naming the gap matters.
Say: "Honestly naming the gap between what has been achieved and what remains is the foundation of the next strategic phase. Organisations that settle for a vague awareness of more to do make little purposeful progress. Name the remaining work specifically, then plan for it."
(Insight: Naming the gap. Source: Journal, 10 April 2026 — Professional Insights: Strategy)

§5. Read the room.
Take one first answer for each domain if the room offers them. Note which domain is named most often. Tell the groups: test that domain hardest when you write your SiP in Section 4.

§6. Bridge to Section 4.
Say: "We now have two tests for any Success in Practice: depth within each domain and balance across all four. In Section 4 each group builds its own outputs and applies both tests to its Success in Practice."

§ON THE PORTAL, AFTER THE TEACHING:
Participants write the reflection in Section 3 of the participant file: 3.1 Reflection — SiP Indicators.

slides.title: Section 5 Reflections
slides.notes:
§SECTION 5 REFLECTIONS

§HOW TO USE THIS SLIDE:

§1. Show the slide and read the prompt aloud.
5.2 Reflection — Application: "Having completed the full application exercise — what is the single most important shift your organisation must make to close the gap between your current strategic capability and the SiP you have collectively described?"

§2. Say what the reflection is for.
Point learners to the portal section that they will be required to complete with as much depth as possible. The reflections build the learning portfolio they receive at the end of the programme.
Say: "You write this reflection on the portal after the teaching, once the application exercise is complete, with as much depth as you can."

§3. Set the standard.
Say: "Name one shift only. Name it as a change in a decision, a capability or a behaviour. Say which gap it closes between your current strategic capability and the SiP your group described, and what your own role must do first."
Listen for: a list of five shifts. It is a sign that the participant has yet to choose.

§4. Say why the shift must reach behaviour.
Say: "Organisations often rebuild structures without correcting the behaviours that caused the original failure. Recovery is temporary when the underlying assumptions, relationships and compromises remain unchanged."
(Insight: Rebuilding without correcting. Source: Journal, 2 August 2026 — Professional Insights: Strategy)

§5. Bridge to the Unit Summary.
Say: "We close the unit by returning to where we started."

§ON THE PORTAL, AFTER THE TEACHING:
Participants write the reflection in Section 5 of the participant file: 5.2 Reflection — Application.
